content:
With the launch of the new iPhone Duo, Apple has taken something of a gamble on the software side. All apps will need to be recompiled to iOS 27.0 at minimum to take advantage of the iPhone Duo's larger internal display. To use Duo's distinctive new tab bar and other interface elements will require an upgrade to iOS 27.1.

Of course, this means a lot of developers will need to rebuild their apps to support Duo. But on the flip side, Apple is also taking a risk: many apps on the iPhone Duo may end up stuck in letterbox mode.

An obvious solution would be to let Apple allow those resizable iPad binaries to run on the iPhone Duo. The trade-off is that the experience might feel a bit rough. If there's a compatibility layer in place, many developers may also take longer to support the iPhone Duo interface elements.

I understand why Apple isn't doing this, because the interface they've designed for the iPhone Duo really does feel intuitive and carefully polished. If Apple supported resizable iPad apps, the whole device would end up feeling not much different from a typical Android foldable.

That said, you can't help but wonder how many developers will need to spend how long just to compile to iOS 27 at the very least. Compiling for iOS 27 isn't just about supporting Duo — it also means you no longer have the option of opting out of Liquid Glass. For developers who aren't prepared, the latter means many of them will drag their feet on updating for the iPhone Duo.

Given that you can use split-screen on the Duo, apps that aren't fully expanded on the inner screen may not be the biggest issue — provided Apple supports split-screen for non-native apps.

That said, for mobile gaming — which I'm sure will be hugely popular on the iPhone Duo's inner screen — the lack of a true full-screen experience will put a lot of users off.

I do hope Apple's efforts to encourage developers to support the Duo interface pay off, but I am genuinely concerned. Obviously, only time will tell.

Worst case, Apple could simply add an iPad app compatibility mode for the iPhone Duo in iOS 28, which would both improve the user experience and secure a first wave of app support.

I'm really looking forward to the iPhone Duo, but this gamble of Apple asking developers to support both Liquid Glass and Duo at the same time may make the first few months a rather rough experience.

Would you buy an iPhone Duo? What are you most looking forward to? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
